newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daiwa Bank says hopes to eventually return to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Daiwa Bank says hopes to eventually return to U.S..

text.p: Daiwa Bank Ltd said on Wednesday it hopes to resume operations in the United States, but the timing of its possible reentry into the U.S. market has not yet been decided.
"We have always been hoping to resume our U.S. operations when we are allowed to do so, but we don't have any time schedule at the moment," said a bank spokesman.
The business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Wednesday that the bank aims to reopen its office in New York as early as 1999, but to limit operations to business with Japanese companies.
Daiwa Bank was forced to halt its U.S. operations in February 1996 because of a scandal involving a coverup of a huge loss from trading in U.S. bonds.
Daiwa Bank pleaded guilty to 16 charges that it covered up a $1.1 billion loss in unauthorised trading at its New York branch and was fined a record $340 million by U.S. authorities.
A three-year ban on it operating in the U.S. runs until February 1999.
